validity.researcher_notes: gem.wiki returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) so wiki_citations.json is empty for this row per the batch's known harvest failure; went straight to open-web research. Two independent DAWN.COM news reports, 7 years apart, both describe the exact physical route GEM records (StartLocation Pir Koh -> EndLocation Sui): (1) DAWN 31-Aug-2007 'Gas pipeline blown up, 14 arrested in Sui' reports a bombing that damaged 'the 16-inch diameter gas pipeline connecting three wells of the Sui gas field and the Pir Koh gas field with the Sui purification plant,' attributed to a DPO statement, and identifies the line as 'a main pipeline of the Pakistan Petroleum Limited (PPL)'. (2) DAWN 27-Jan-2014 (news/1083050) reports a second, separate attack on 'the pipeline supplying natural gas to Sui purification plant from well number 41 of Pir Koh gas-field.' These are two independently reported incidents (different dates, different specific well/segment, different bylines/officials cited), not one wire story reprinted, and neither traces back to GEM. Checked the 63-row Pakistan-gas roster for a relabel/duplicate risk: no other row names Pir Koh, and no other Sindh/Balochistan field-line row plausibly matches this Pir Koh-to-Sui route, so no duplicate flag. Wikipedia's Sui gas field article independently corroborates that PPL (not SNGPL) operates the Sui field/purification plant, and clarifies SNGPL/SSGC are downstream transmission-distribution utilities, not field operators -- consistent with the DAWN attribution below. Caveat: both existence sources are security-incident news reports rather than company or regulatory documentation, and the most recent is from 2014 -- no fresher confirmation of continued operating status was found (search-engine access was heavily degraded this session: WebSearch quota was exhausted, Bing/Google returned generic/blocked pages, and DuckDuckGo HTML search hit a CAPTCHA after the first two queries, so corroboration is thinner than the SOP target of clean multi-outlet coverage).

validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's Owner1 is 'Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Ltd (SNGPL)' at 100%. That is contradicted by the only source that names an owner for this specific pipeline: DAWN 31-Aug-2007 explicitly identifies the damaged line as 'a main pipeline of the Pakistan Petroleum Limited (PPL)', and describes it as connecting Sui-field wells and the Pir Koh gas field to the 'Sui purification plant' -- PPL's own processing facility. SNGPL is Pakistan's northern-region gas TRANSMISSION AND DISTRIBUTION utility (moves processed sales gas onward to consumers); it has no documented role at the Sui/Pir Koh wellhead-to-plant gathering system. Wikipedia's Sui gas field article corroborates that PPL operates the Sui field/plant and separately names SNGPL/SSGC only as downstream distribution companies, i.e. a different tier of the value chain. This looks like a bulk-load misattribution (the batch's LastUpdated=2023-07-07 bulk-load pattern flagged in scope notes) rather than a documented ownership fact. Not staging a fill for the current SNGPL value since I believe it is incorrect; flagging for Update instead per the no-auto-apply rule.

validity.researcher_notes: Both DAWN articles describe this exact line as connecting production WELLS (Sui-field wells, and separately Pir Koh well no. 41) to the Sui PURIFICATION PLANT -- i.e. raw/wet gas gathering from wellheads to a processing facility, the classic gathering-line pattern this batch's scope notes specifically warn is often mislabeled 'transmission' in this bulk load. A 70.5 km, 16-24in field-to-plant line fits that pattern much better than a long-haul transmission trunk moving already-processed gas between hubs/distribution networks.
